name: toggle-group
purpose: ToggleGroup is a connected group of buttons that picks exactly one value out of a small set of related options, with a selection indicator that slides to the active segment. It renders as a `radiogroup` whose segments are `radio` buttons, is driven by an `options` array plus `v-model`, and works uncontrolled through `defaultValue`. It differs from `tabs`, which switches between content panels it owns: a segmented button only holds the chosen value and leaves rendering what that value means to the consumer.
useWhen: Use ToggleGroup (segmented control) to switch a view or mode in place (Table/Chart, 1h/24h), with two to five short segments; it is not a form field. For one choice in a form use RadioGroup; for an on/off setting use Switch; for the theme in app chrome use ThemeSwitcher.
Switch in place between two to five related modes, views or ranges (a time range, a list/grid view, a filter scope) where exactly one is always active.
Offer a compact single choice in a toolbar or a card header where a radio list would take too much room.
Show a choice that is currently unavailable as a disabled segment instead of hiding it; mark it `locked` when it is unavailable because of a plan or a permission.
avoidWhen: The choice switches between content panels that belong to the control → use `tabs`.
The choice is a form field with a label, helper text or validation → use `radio-group` (`variant="card"` when each option needs a description).
The value is a binary on/off setting → use `switch` (in a horizontal `field` inside a form).
The user can pick more than one option → use `checkbox` (in a horizontal `field`).
The control triggers an action instead of holding a value → use `button` or `split-button`.
related: `tabs` — tabs that own their panels; reach for it when each option reveals its own content region.
`radio-group` — the form-field single choice; `variant="card"` when each option carries a description.
`theme-switcher` — the system / light / dark choice in app chrome.
`button` — a lone action; the segments here hold a value instead of firing one.

Naming: Radix and shadcn `ToggleGroup` is a group of `aria-pressed` toggles with `type="single" | "multiple"`. This component is the single-select segmented control (Cloudscape and Geist call it a segmented control): one value is always selected and the segments are radios. There is no multiple mode; for several independent toggles use `checkbox`es or `ButtonGroup` toggles.
bestPractices: Keep labels to one or two words. When the options do not fit their container they flow onto another row, and a label breaks across lines only when one option alone is wider than the group; a label is never cut off.
Give every option a unique `value`; values are coerced to strings and used as the list key and the selection identity, so duplicates collide.
Pass `ariaLabel` whenever no visible label names the group.
Use `fluid` to make the group fill a narrow container and share its width across segments, instead of styling the width at the call site.
Bind `v-model` when the selection lives in the parent; use `defaultValue` only to seed an uncontrolled group.

props.name: options
props.type: `ToggleGroupOption[]` (`{ label?: string | number; value?: string | number; disabled?: boolean; locked?: boolean; icon?: string }`)
props.doc: Segmented choices shown as a mutually exclusive group.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when no visible group label is associated.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial selection when `v-model` is not set.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token, on the same 28 / 32 / 40 rhythm every other control uses.

props.name: fluid
props.doc: Stretches the group to its container and lets the options share that width.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables every option of the group.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name. Set, a hidden input carries the selected value so a native `form` submits it; `disabled` leaves it out.

props.name: showLabels
props.doc: Shows each option's label beside its icon. Set false for icon-only segments: the label stays as the option's accessible name and its hover title.
